title: The cycle class of a Cartier divisor
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an integer $r\geq1$, and a finite commutative $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$-algebra $\Lambda$. Let $Z$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $i:D\hookrightarrow Z$ be an effective Cartier divisor, meaning that its ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Use the ordinary small pro-etale module derived category $D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with the pro-etale module inverse image $g^*$, closed direct image $i_*$ and adjunction unit $\Lambda_Z\to i_*i^*\Lambda_Z=i_*\Lambda_D$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]. Write $\nu_Z:Z_{\mathrm{proét}}\to Z_{\mathrm{ét}}$ for the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], put $\mu_{\ell^r}=\ker((-)^{\ell^r}:\mathbf G_m\to\mathbf G_m)$ on the etale site [sk-def-kummer], and use the finite Tate line
$$\Lambda_Z(1)=\nu_Z^*(\mu_{\ell^r}\otimes_{R_Z}\Lambda_Z),$$
with the sheaf tensor product and finite etale Tate line of [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. The roots projection of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] canonically identifies this line for larger killing exponents; the morphism below is independent of that exponent. This is the finite twist, with derived pullback as in [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Define $c_1(\mathcal O_Z(D))$ by the etale Kummer boundary of the generator torsor of $\mathcal O_Z(D)$ [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor, lem-sc-torsor-h1, lem-amb-kummer-any-base], followed by derived extension from $R$ to $\Lambda$ and by $\nu_Z^*$. There is a canonical morphism
$$c_D:i_*\Lambda_D\longrightarrow\Lambda_Z(1)[2]$$
whose composite with the adjunction unit $\Lambda_Z\to i_*\Lambda_D$ is $c_1(\mathcal O_Z(D))$. For every homomorphism $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ of finite commutative $R$-algebras, derived extension of scalars carries $c_{D,\Lambda}$ to $c_{D,\Lambda'}$ under the canonical supported-constant and Tate-line identifications. For every $g:Z'\to Z$ for which $D'=D\times_ZZ'$ remains an effective Cartier divisor, put $i':D'\hookrightarrow Z'$ and $g_D:D'\to D$. The canonical exchange $g^*i_*\Lambda_D\xrightarrow{\sim}i'_*g_D^*\Lambda_D=i'_*\Lambda_{D'}$ and the canonical finite Tate-line pullback identify $g^*c_{D,\Lambda}$ with $c_{D',\Lambda}$.

proof.text: Work first on $Z_{\mathrm{ét}}$ and put $n=\ell^r$. Choose a Zariski covering $U_a$ with regular equations $t_a$ for $D$, and let $j:Z\setminus D\hookrightarrow Z$. Inside $j_*\mathbf G_m$ define $\mathcal M_D$ to be the subsheaf locally generated by $\mathbf G_m$ and $t_a^{-1}$, allowing all integral powers. On an etale chart the pulled-back $t_a$ is still regular: an etale ring map is flat, so tensor its injective multiplication-by-$t_a$ map with that ring. Consequently restriction of units to the complement is injective. If $t_b=v_{ab}t_a$ with $v_{ab}$ a unit, then $t_b^{-1}=v_{ab}^{-1}t_a^{-1}$; thus the locally specified subsheaves agree, and sheaf gluing defines $\mathcal M_D$ globally. This construction allows arbitrary pole orders, not just a simple pole.

source.place: Paragraphs 2 and 3: construct the Cartier extension sheaf

proof.text:
Define $q:\mathcal M_D\to i_*\mathbf Z_D$ by $q(ut_a^{-b})=b$ along $D$ and zero off $D$. The change-of-equation formula in step 1 preserves $b$. At a geometric point outside $D$, $t_a$ is a unit and $\mathcal M_D=\mathbf G_m$. At a geometric point on $D$, a relation $ut_a^{-b}=vt_a^{-c}$ with $b>c$ would, after clearing a power of $t_a$ and cancelling it by regularity on an etale neighbourhood, make $t_a^{b-c}$ a unit; its value at the point is zero, a contradiction. Hence the exponent is unique there. Every integer lifts locally as $t_a^{-b}$, and exponent zero gives exactly the units. The closed immersion is finite: on an affine chart its ring is $A/(t_a)$, a cyclic finite $A$-module. The finite-stalk formula for this immersion identifies the quotient stalks with those of $i_*\mathbf Z_D$ (one copy of $\mathbf Z$ on $D$, zero elsewhere). Exactness and conservativity of geometric stalks therefore prove
$$0\to\mathbf G_m\to\mathcal M_D\xrightarrow{q}i_*\mathbf Z_D\to0.\tag{G1}$$
The same stalk calculation proves that multiplication by $n$ on $F=i_*\mathbf Z_D$ is injective and $F/nF\cong i_*R_D$.

The exact Kummer sequence applies on $Z$, since $n=\ell^r$ is invertible. Thus multiplication by $n$ on $B=\mathbf G_m$ is an epimorphism with kernel $\mu_n$. Apply [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction] to (G1), with the injectivity on $F$ proved in step 2. Its actual derived scalar-extension functor gives a morphism in $D(Z_{\mathrm{ét}},R)$,
$$d_{D,R}:i_*R_D\longrightarrow\mu_n[2].$$
In particular this step constructs an $R$-linear derived morphism, rather than inferring $R$-linearity from an underlying morphism of abelian derived objects. The shift is $[2]$: the Kummer kernel is in degree $-1$ of $B\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}R$, and the extension boundary has the additional shift $[1]$.

source.place: Paragraph 4: reduce the extension boundary modulo n

proof.text: For $s:\mathbf Z_Z\to i_*\mathbf Z_D$ the restriction map sending $1$ to $1$, the sheaf of its lifts in (G1) has local generators $t_a^{-1}$. Multiplication by units identifies this lift torsor with the generator torsor of $\mathcal O_Z(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$: on overlaps the generator $t_b^{-1}$ is $v_{ab}^{-1}$ times $t_a^{-1}$, exactly the transition for the dual of the ideal generator. Its extension boundary is its torsor class by [lem-sc-torsor-h1]. More explicitly, the free-abelian extension used in that statement maps to the pullback of (G1) along $s$, by sending the symbol of a lift to that lift; the relations $[u\cdot t]=[t]+u$ are preserved. It is an isomorphism locally on each chosen generator. The normalization clause of [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction] therefore says that $d_{D,R}$ precomposed with $R_Z\to i_*R_D$ is the Kummer first Chern class of $\mathcal O_Z(D)$. This also fixes its sign. Changing the equations changes the local generator by a unit, hence gives the same torsor and the same class.

source.place: Paragraph 5: identify the composite with the Chern class

proof.text:
Apply derived extension of scalars from $R$ to $\Lambda$ to $d_{D,R}$. Specify its source comparison $\alpha_\Lambda:(i_*R_D)\otimes_R^L\Lambda\to i_*\Lambda_D$ as the adjunct, under derived extension/restriction, of the map $i_*R_D\to\operatorname{Res}(i_*\Lambda_D)$ induced by $R_D\to\Lambda_D$. Direct image commutes with coefficient restriction by its sectionwise definition. At each geometric stalk $i_*R_D$ is either $R$ or zero, so its derived tensor is respectively $\Lambda$ or zero, and $\alpha_\Lambda$ is respectively $x\otimes a\mapsto xa$ or the zero-object identity. Stalks commute with this derived tensor calculation by inverse-image monoidality and the identification of stalks with geometric-point inverse image. Exactness and conservativity of stalks, applied to the cohomology sheaves of the cone of $\alpha_\Lambda$, prove that this specified comparison is an isomorphism. Its target is $(\mu_n\otimes_R\Lambda)[2]$ because the finite etale Tate-line theorem makes $\mu_n$ locally free of rank one, hence its one-term complex is K-flat. Denote the resulting map by $d_{D,\Lambda}$. Applying this functor to the equation of step 4 proves its Chern-class equation. For $R\to\Lambda\to\Lambda'$, the composite extension-of-scalars functor and extension directly from $R$ are canonically the same: each is left adjoint to the same composite termwise restriction functor. The adjunctions are the ones in [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], and their units send $x$ to $1\otimes x$. Thus the comparison sends $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes ab$ on tensor models, and carries $d_{D,\Lambda}$ to $d_{D,\Lambda'}$. No flatness of either coefficient map is assumed. For independence of the exponent, replace $n=\ell^r$ by $m=\ell^s$ with $s\geq r$. Write $R_m=\mathbf Z/m$ and $R_n=R$. Composition of the scalar-extension adjunctions gives a natural isomorphism of $D(R_n)$-valued functors
$$(-\otimes_{R_m}^L R_n)\circ(-\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^L R_m)\simeq-\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^L R_n.$$
Naturality of this isomorphism at the extension boundary already compares the two constructed morphisms inside $D(R_n)$. To identify its source and target sheaf comparisons, the chain map from the two-term free resolution $[\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{m}\mathbf Z]$ to $[\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{n}\mathbf Z]$ has degree-zero map $1$ and degree-minus-one map $m/n$: its chain equation is $n(m/n)=m$. After tensoring with $B=\mathbf G_m$, it induces on $H^{-1}$ the power map $\mu_m\to\mu_n$, $z\mapsto z^{m/n}$. On $F$ it induces the quotient $F/mF\to F/nF$. This computes the transitivity comparison just specified: its adjunct is the quotient-induced scalar-extension unit, represented by that free-resolution map. Since $\mu_m$ is locally free over $R_m$ and $F/mF=i_*R_{m,D}$ has the stalkwise flatness already checked, both sides are concentrated in degree $-1$ for $B$ and degree $0$ for $F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], and shifting both sides by the same integer, a morphism between two sheaves in the same degree is determined by its map of sheaves. Thus the calculation identifies the module-derived comparison with the roots-projection and quotient identifications, without testing equality of general derived morphisms after forgetting scalars. Naturality of transitivity now proves that extension of $d_{D,\mathbf Z/m}$ to $R$ is $d_{D,R}$ under the roots-projection identification. Its extension to $\Lambda$ is consequently the same map as before, proving independence of the chosen killing exponent.

source.place: Paragraph 4, final sentences: finite coefficient extension and its functoriality

proof.text: Let $g:Z'\to Z$ be as in the statement. The pulled equations $g^*t_a$ are regular by the hypothesis that $D'$ is still effective Cartier. Pullback of units and the assignment $t_a^{-1}\mapsto(g^*t_a)^{-1}$ give a map $g^{-1}\mathcal M_D\to\mathcal M_{D'}$; the formula $t_b^{-1}=v_{ab}^{-1}t_a^{-1}$ pulls back to the corresponding formula on $Z'$, so the local maps glue. The canonical closed exchange $g^{-1}i_*\mathbf Z_D\to i'_*\mathbf Z_{D'}$ is an isomorphism: at a geometric point of $Z'$ both stalks are $\mathbf Z$, with map the identity, when its image lies in $D$, and both are zero otherwise. Use the finite-stalk formula, constant-sheaf pullback, and the stalk-as-inverse-image description. Exact inverse image makes this a morphism from the pullback of (G1) to (G1) for $D'$. Naturality of [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction] identifies the reduced boundary maps under this exchange and the roots-of-unity comparison of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Monoidality of derived inverse image then commutes this identity with extension to $\Lambda$. This proves the asserted etale base-change identity, with the canonical exchange map, including nonflat $g$ whenever $D'$ remains Cartier.

source.place: Paragraph 6: pull back equations and the extension; identify the closed exchange

proof.text:
Now apply the exact derived comparison inverse image $
u_Z^*$ to $d_{D,\Lambda}$. A closed immersion is finite, quasi-compact and quasi-separated (affine locally it is $A	o A/I$, a finite cyclic $A$-module). Its etale direct image is exact by the finite-direct-image theorem, also for constant-ring modules since exactness is detected on their underlying abelian sheaves. The comparison theorem for qcqs direct images therefore gives
$$
u_Z^*(i_*\Lambda_D)=
u_Z^*Ri_{\mathrm{ét},*}\Lambda_D\simeq Ri_{\mathrm{proét},*}
u_D^*\Lambda_D.$$
The left side is a degree-zero sheaf. On the chosen small pro-etale site, the module category is Grothendieck by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Pro-etale module direct image is left exact, and the degree-zero resolution theorem identifies $\mathcal H^0(Ri_*\Lambda_D)$ with $i_*\Lambda_D$: for a nonnegative injective resolution $I$ this is $\ker(i_*I^0	o i_*I^1)=i_*\ker(I^0	o I^1)$. Taking degree zero of the right side is therefore ordinary direct image, so this identifies the source canonically with $i_{\mathrm{proét},*}\Lambda_D$, and identifies its adjunction unit with the unit on the pro-etale site. The target is $\Lambda_Z(1)[2]$ by the finite Tate-line definition in the statement. Let $c_{D,\Lambda}$ be this transported map. Applying $
u_Z^*$ to the equation in step 5 proves its required composite equation. Only bounded-below objects enter the direct-image comparison: the source and the unshifted Tate line are degree-zero sheaves.

source.place: Paragraph 1: pass from the etale construction to the pro-etale site

proof.text:
The inverse-image square in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] identifies $g_{\mathrm{proét}}^*
u_Z^*$ with $
u_{Z'}^*g_{\mathrm{ét}}^*$. The same node makes its direct-image comparisons compatible with units and counits. Write $K=\Lambda_D$ and $e:g^*Ri_*K	o Ri'_*(g_D^*K)$ for exchange. Its adjoint is explicitly
$$i'^*g^*Ri_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}g_D^*i^*Ri_*K\xrightarrow{g_D^*\varepsilon_i}g_D^*K,$$
where the first arrow is inverse-image commutation and $\varepsilon_i$ is the counit. Applying $
u_{D'}^*$ to this composite, inverse-image commutation identifies the first arrow with the pro-etale inverse-image commutation, and counit compatibility identifies the second with $g_{D,\mathrm{proét}}^*\varepsilon_{i,\mathrm{proét}}$. This is exactly the adjoint formula defining pro-etale exchange; adjunction bijectivity proves equality of the exchange maps. Applying $
u_{Z'}^*$ to the equality of step 6 therefore gives the base-change identity in the statement. For coefficients, the general ringed-topos derived tensor comparison applied to $
u$ commutes pullback with scalar extension; the constant rings pull back to the constant rings by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. The source comparison $\alpha_\Lambda$ of step 5 is preserved too: its adjunct is induced by $R_D	o\Lambda_D$, and comparison preserves that map and the scalar-extension adjunction unit. For two coefficient maps, the tensor associativity comparison sends $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes ab$; inverse image gives that identical formula. Hence applying $
u_Z^*$ to the coefficient identity of step 5 gives precisely the asserted coefficient identity. These are equalities of the constructed morphisms, obtained by functoriality, without using stalks to test equality of derived morphisms.

split_report.summary: Followed the six-paragraph Cartier-extension route. Filled all notion dependencies, proved gluing and local exponent exactness, isolated one general derived-reduction lemma, computed the Chern sign via the lift torsor, and verified arbitrary finite coefficient maps and Cartier-preserving base change through canonical comparisons. Repaired the unbound coefficient symbol by making the source proof's finite commutative Z/ell^r-algebra scope explicit. No Lean edits or compilation.

Statement: binding Lambda to a finite commutative Z/ell^r-algebra is accepted. It matches proof paragraph 4, the chapter's layer (A), def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules (finite discrete Lambda) and every DAG citer (tower levels Z/ell^n, scalar-six with a common exponent, p1-cohomology with the same binder). The Chern equation is kept. Coefficient change covers arbitrary maps of finite commutative R-algebras, flat or not. Base change still covers every g keeping D' Cartier, and no target is touched. Steps 1-8 are correct. (1) Etale flatness keeps t_a regular and the transitions glue. (2) Regularity gives a well-defined exponent; the immersion is finite, stalks are Z or 0, so n is mono on F and F/nF = i_*R_D. (3) n is invertible, so the Kummer sequence gives n-epi on G_m and the new lemma gives d: i_*R_D -> mu_n[2] in D(R). (4) The lift torsor is Isom(O, O(D)) via the dual generators; E_T -> s^*M_D is an iso of extensions, so the adjunct formula gives c_1 with its sign. (5) alpha_Lambda is an iso on stalks and mu_n is flat, hence K-flat. Exponent independence was checked with the chain map (m/n, 1) and the SES map z -> z^{m/n}, so kappa_n = power[1] o kappa_m. (6) D' Cartier makes g^*t_a a nonzerodivisor, using only the canonical map g^{-1}G_m -> G_m'. (7) Finite qcqs i plus the comparison theorem, with H^0 from left exactness and enough injectives. (8) The mate formula holds with unit/counit compatibility. New node lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction is true: [Z -n-> Z] gives F/nF[0] and H[1]; the adjunct normalization fixes the iso uniquely; naturality of the unit gives the kappa formula. Small cases n=1, a split S and dropped hypotheses agree.
